subject: DONE s323d: getlogin builtin (Data-Dump dd.t)
description:
FIXED s323d.  Data-Dump's dd.t died with "The function main::pl-getlogin is undefined" — the last cheap cause on the widened CPAN board.

FOUR edits, the usual builtin family:
  cl/pcl-runtime.lisp  — `p-getlogin` defun
  cl/pcl-runtime.lisp  — `#:p-getlogin` in the :pcl export list
  Pl/PExpr/Config.pm   — `getlogin => 0` arity
  Pl/ExprToCL.pm       — the builtin-NAME list (~line 158)
The last one is the one that is easy to miss: it decides `p-` vs `pl-` emission.  With only the first three the call still came out as `(pl-getlogin)` — a user-sub call — and still crashed.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTE: perl documents getlogin as unreliable and tells you to prefer `getpwuid($<)`; PCL takes that advice, because SBCL exposes no getlogin(3) and the effective-uid lookup is what real callers want.  undef when the uid has no passwd entry, as in perl.

Gate-verified only (125 files / 4476 PASS): no perl-tests file uses getlogin, so the full sweep adds nothing here — it runs with the next batch per the s323 cadence rule.
